user.text: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.

history.assistant:

360	#### Keeping the page interactive
361	
362	While a transition runs, the `::view-transition` overlay captures pointer events, so clicks during the animation are lost. Let them pass through to the live page:
363

370	This restores interactivity for unnamed content. Hit-testing still skips named participants (like the anchored header) for the transition's duration, so keep transitions short and avoid naming elements the user clicks rapidly.
371	
372	#### Respecting reduced motion
373	
374	Directional slides simulate physical movement across the viewport. This is the most common trigger for motion sensitivity. Morphs, reveals, and crossfades carry less risk since they affect smaller areas or rely on opacity rather than position.
375	
376	The simplest approach is to disable all animation durations:
377	
378	```css filename="app/globals.css"
379	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
380	  ::view-transition-old(*),
381	  ::view-transition-new(*),
382	  ::view-transition-group(*) {
383	    animation-duration: 0s !important;
384	    animation-delay: 0s !important;
385	  }
386	}
387	```
388	
389	Without animation, content swaps instantly, which is the browser's default behavior. A more refined approach would preserve crossfades and opacity transitions while removing positional movement. See ["No Motion Isn't Always prefers-reduced-motion"](https://css-tricks.com/nuking-motion-with-prefers-reduced-motion/) for more on this.

391	### Step 4: Crossfade content within the same route
392	
393	The gallery has a photographer section with tabs. Each tab shows a different photographer's photos, but the route structure is the same: `/collection/[slug]`. Clicking between tabs does not feel like navigating to a new page. It feels like switching content within the same container.
394	
395	A directional slide would be wrong here. Slides communicate "going to a new place." A crossfade communicates "same place, different content." The container persists (continuity), only the grid inside changes (swap).
396	
397	Use a `ViewTransition` with `key` set to the current slug. When the key changes, React triggers a transition between the old and new content:
398	
399	```tsx filename="app/collection/[slug]/page.tsx"

407	      <ViewTransition
408	        key={slug}
409	        name="collection-content"
410	        share="auto"
411	        enter="auto"
412	        default="none"
413	      >
414	        <CollectionGrid slug={slug} />
415	      </ViewTransition>
416	    </Suspense>
417	  )
418	}
